title: Causal inference and experimentation
stage: College AI and machine learning degree
audience: a college student in an artificial intelligence, machine learning or computer science degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn to answer cause-and-effect questions with data: potential outcomes and causal effects, randomized experiments and A/B tests, power and sample size, causal graphs, d-separation and the backdoor criterion, confounding and adjustment, propensity scores, matching and weighting, instrumental variables, difference-in-differences and regression discontinuity, heterogeneous effects, and how causal reasoning improves machine learning models and evaluations.
primary_reading: Causal Inference: What If by Hernán and Robins (free PDF)

weeks.2: Average treatment effects and the fundamental problem of causal inference
weeks.4: Power, sample size and experiment pitfalls
weeks.12: Causality in machine learning: shortcuts, distribution shift and fairness

blocks.deliverable: Compute effects from a table of potential outcomes.
Compute the sample size for an A/B test.
Find valid adjustment sets in four causal graphs.
Week 7 midterm; estimate an effect by inverse probability weighting.
Explain a shortcut a classifier learned using a causal graph.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Causal analysis memo: for a supplied observational data set about a treatment and an outcome, draw and defend a causal graph, choose an adjustment set, estimate the effect by stratification and by inverse probability weighting, run one sensitivity check, and write a memo for a decision maker that states the estimate, its assumptions and what a randomized experiment would add.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
